title: URLs: scheme, host, path, query, fragment
learningObjectives: Explain urls: scheme, host, path, query, fragment and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: A URL identifies a resource and may contain a scheme, host, port, path, query string, and fragment. The scheme describes how the resource is accessed; the query carries parameters; the fragment identifies a location or client-side state within the resource.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct URL reading helps build safe links, troubleshoot routing, and understand API endpoints. Query values are input, not trusted authorization.
understand.analogy: A URL is a structured address with separate fields for protocol, destination, route, options, and in-page location.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The URL API parses each component into a separate property.

examples.explanation: The URL API parses each component into a separate property.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the concept; some browser examples require a real served page and supported APIs.

practise.guidedTask: Parse a URL and label each component. Change one query parameter using URLSearchParams without manually concatenating strings.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
hints: Use browser developer tools to inspect actual behaviour.
Test with keyboard and different viewport sizes.
Keep core content available when enhancements are unsupported.
